tasks.short: Help managers and employees understand their contracts and sort out problems at work.

today.trigger: A manager or employee raises a question, contractual disagreement or workplace problem through Outlook, Teams or a site conversation.
steps: Hear the question and establish what happened, including the employee's account.
Check the relevant AFAS record, contract, CAO and SharePoint policy.
Speak with the manager, employee or specialist to clarify missing facts.
Explain the position, agree the next action and document the case.
Follow up with the people involved.
drudgery: Finding the right contract and CAO clause
Writing repetitive case summaries and follow-up notes
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline: 60 minutes of HRBP work per case, excluding elapsed waiting time. Record gathering and documentation take about 25 minutes; conversations and judgment take the rest.

lenses.faster: Record searching, timeline assembly and first drafts largely disappear; the HRBP checks sources and still hears both sides. A representative case falls from 60 to 39 minutes, including review and follow-up.
lenses.autonomous: An HRBP opens a case and authorizes a fixed preparation workflow that retrieves permitted records and drafts a sourced brief. The HRBP verifies the facts and decides what to say or do before anything reaches the employee or manager.
lenses.ambitious: Group served for the first time: night-shift supervisors receive scheduled case advice without waiting for daytime office hours. Demand would grow as preparation gets cheaper, although sensitive conversations still require HRBP availability.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding email histories or copying contract clauses. The HRBP gets more time to listen, repair working relationships and help managers act fairly.
lenses.options: Compare a clarified expectation, a voluntary working arrangement and a formal process against the same facts and CAO constraints. These alternatives can change the remedy by exposing consequences for the employee, team and precedent.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward complex cases and early intervention, with delegated authority to resolve routine disputes within agreed limits. The job becomes more expert in Dutch employment practice and conflict resolution.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's case-summary preparation after learning AFAS record handling, access controls and retention rules.
Absorb initial absence-process deadline checks from the HR Administrator after learning Wet verbetering poortwachter milestones; medical judgments remain with the occupational health professionals.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP must hear conflicting accounts, notice power imbalances, earn trust and judge a fair response. The person remains responsible for contractual interpretation in disputed cases, mediation and any employment consequence.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: one model call turns a permitted evidence bundle into a checkable case brief inside a fixed workflow; the conversations and resolution stay with the HRBP.

in_practice.trigger: The HRBP creates a case reference and selects the records allowed for preparation.
steps: Retrieve the selected AFAS fields, contract, relevant CAO sections and case correspondence through approved access.
Separate verified facts, conflicting accounts and missing information.
Draft a timeline, source-linked explanation and questions for the HRBP.
Have the HRBP check the brief and conduct the necessary conversations.
Record the approved action and follow-up date in the restricted case record.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves every case explanation, communication and action; contested facts, complaints, absence cases and disciplinary matters receive direct human handling.
systems: AFAS Profit through an approved integration or controlled export
data_needed: Minimum necessary employee and employment fields
Selected correspondence and verified case facts
Absence-process dates where relevant, excluding diagnoses and clinical records
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint case record containing source references, draft version, HRBP corrections, approved action and follow-up date.

evidence.claim: IBM reports an HR front door that escalates complex cases to HRBPs, supporting the separation of routine questions from human casework.
Source-linked case preparation is technically plausible, but the proposed 35% saving is an unvalidated estimate for Noordhaven.

risks: A plausible summary could omit the employee's account or treat an allegation as established fact.
The wrong CAO, contract version or site arrangement could produce incorrect advice.
Personnel-data arrangements may require OR consent; important technology changes may also require OR advice.
AVG/GDPR controls must prevent excessive case access, inappropriate retention and processing of medical information.
research_questions: Across a sample of cases, how much active HRBP time goes into gathering records versus listening and resolving the issue?
Can AFAS and SharePoint supply source-linked records while enforcing case-specific permissions?
Can the workflow reliably distinguish verified facts, allegations and missing evidence?
Will managers, employees and the OR accept this preparation method without reducing trust in case handling?

tasks.short: Explain our HR policies, CAOs and employment rules to employees and managers.

today.trigger: An employee or manager asks how a policy, CAO provision or employment rule applies.
steps: Clarify the question and whether it concerns general guidance or a personal case.
Find the current policy, applicable CAO and relevant legal guidance.
Check site, worker category and any exceptions.
Explain the answer and send the supporting source.
Escalate ambiguous interpretation or record a policy gap.
drudgery: Answering the same leave, allowance and procedure questions
Rephrasing formal language into a usable answer
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline: 20 minutes per question averaged across routine answers and exceptions. Search, applicability checks and writing dominate routine questions.

lenses.faster: An approved policy assistant answers routine questions with citations, removing most searching and repeated writing. Exception handling, content maintenance and sampled review leave an average of seven HRBP minutes per question against an illustrative 20-minute baseline.
lenses.autonomous: A question starts a fixed retrieval-and-answer workflow that uses released content and predefined applicability rules. It sends general guidance automatically, while personal disputes, uncertain applicability and unsupported answers go to the HRBP.
lenses.ambitious: Group served for the first time: flex workers and night shifts receive accessible guidance on site procedures and where employment questions should go. Demand would grow because people could ask at the moment they need an answer, with agency contract questions routed to the agency.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss repeating policy text or hunting for the latest version. The HRBP spends more time explaining difficult exceptions and fixing policies that repeatedly confuse people.
lenses.options: The assistant can show examples for different worker categories or proposed working arrangements without choosing one for the employee. Seeing those differences can change a manager's proposed arrangement before a personal case needs HR review.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP spends fewer hours answering routine questions and more hours deciding policy exceptions and recommending clearer provisions. Delegated interpretation rights become explicit, and the role becomes more expert in resolving ambiguity.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's general policy-question intake after learning content publishing, routing and service measurement.
Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's policy-explainer drafting after learning accessible writing and checking comprehension.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP must decide disputed interpretations, reconcile conflicting CAO or contractual provisions and explain consequential exceptions with empathy. The person owns advice that could affect pay, leave, discipline or employment rights.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: a fixed workflow retrieves approved passages and uses one model call to produce a cited answer; deterministic checks and escalation rules make an open-ended agent unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: A worker or manager submits a question through an approved Teams or shared-device interface.
steps: Disclose that the service uses AI and identify the minimum worker category and site needed for general guidance.
Retrieve current, released policy and CAO passages within the user's access rights.
Generate a plain answer with citations and stated applicability.
Send supported general guidance or route personal, ambiguous and unsupported questions to the HRBP.
Review a sample of answers and recurring gaps before releasing revised content.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves the content base and escalation rules before release; each personal or disputed interpretation requires human approval before advice is issued.
data_needed: Versioned policies and both applicable CAOs
Approved legal interpretations and escalation boundaries
Document ownership, effective dates and access permissions
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted HR question register with cited document versions, routing outcome and review findings; minimize or redact personal question text.

evidence.claim: Coca-Cola Andina has a documented HR agent serving employees and creating tickets for questions it cannot answer.
IBM reports substantial HR self-service adoption and human escalation, but its savings cannot be transferred directly to Noordhaven.
A study of Danish workers, including HR professionals, found average chatbot time savings of about 3%, supporting caution about broad productivity forecasts.
The EU AI Act includes transparency obligations for systems interacting directly with people.

risks: A confidently wrong answer could affect contractual rights or pay.
Outdated documents or overlapping CAOs could undermine applicability checks.
Warehouse and flex workers may lack individual Microsoft 365 access or a private place to ask questions.
Personalization can introduce personnel-data processing requiring AVG/GDPR controls and assessment of OR consent rights.
research_questions: What proportion of actual questions can be answered from approved content without accessing an individual's personnel file?
Do tests across both CAOs, three sites and agency workers produce correct citations and reliable escalation?
Can night-shift and flex workers access the service privately and understand its answers?
After content maintenance and exception review, does a pilot remove enough HRBP time to support the 65% estimate?

tasks.short: Help site managers match available people and certified skills to staffing needs.

today.trigger: A site manager raises a staffing gap, seasonal requirement or proposed employee transfer.
steps: Clarify workload, required skills and the period needing cover.
Collect current availability, contract constraints and agency capacity.
Check certificates, working-time constraints and relevant CAO provisions.
Discuss feasible options with managers and affected employees.
Agree the staffing action and coordinate implementation.
drudgery: Rebuilding comparable staffing options in Excel
Chasing current availability across sites and agencies
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline: 120 minutes per staffing review. Preparing comparable options takes about half; checking live facts, preferences and agreement takes the remainder.

lenses.faster: Reusable constraint checks and scenario tables replace spreadsheet rebuilding and much list reconciliation. The HRBP still confirms current availability and discusses choices, reducing an illustrative review from 120 to 84 minutes.
lenses.autonomous: A staffing request prompts the HRBP to run a preparation workbook with approved data and explicit constraints. It flags infeasible options, while the HRBP and site manager choose and approve any assignment or transfer.
lenses.ambitious: Decision made far more often: hold a weekly cross-site review of certificate coverage and internal cover options before agency orders are placed. Demand would grow if preparation became cheap enough to make these reviews useful during seasonal peaks.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss reconciling certificate spreadsheets or recalculating the same cost assumptions. The HRBP gets more time to negotiate workable arrangements and connect staffing needs with employee development.
lenses.options: Compare agency cover, voluntary internal movement and training existing staff using cost, readiness and coverage assumptions. The alternatives can change whether Noordhaven buys temporary capacity or develops permanent capability.
lenses.altitude: The week gains regular capacity discussions across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo instead of mostly reacting to gaps. The HRBP gains delegated authority to propose cross-site cover and training investment within approved limits, making the role more expert in workforce planning.
reach: Absorb the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's routine staffing-scenario assembly after learning data reconciliation and constraint-based modelling.
Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's certificate-gap identification after learning Studytube records and operational certificate requirements.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP and operational manager must judge readiness, employee preferences, local working relationships and operational safety. They must resolve competing site needs and remain accountable for staffing choices.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: the HRBP leads a negotiation with incomplete and changing facts; deterministic checks support scenario preparation without a model ranking employees.

in_practice.trigger: The HRBP receives a staffing request and defines its period, skills and coverage requirements.
steps: Import permitted employment, certificate and agency-capacity data into a controlled workbook.
Confirm current availability with site managers because the nightly extract is insufficient for live allocation.
Apply explicit eligibility and working-time checks to HRBP-defined options.
Compare agency cover, voluntary transfers and training scenarios without scoring employee performance.
Have the HRBP and site manager approve the choice and coordinate it with affected workers.
in_practice.human_gate: Each allocation or transfer requires the authorized manager's approval, HRBP review of constraints and any required employee agreement.
data_needed: Required roles, skills, shifts and coverage periods
Contractual hours and relevant CAO restrictions
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint planning register with input timestamps, scenario assumptions, constraint flags and the manager's approved decision.

evidence.claim: Microsoft describes a Workforce Insights agent giving managers information about organizational structure and staffing.
Explicit certificate and contractual constraints can be checked with deterministic software; the 30% saving is a planning estimate.
The EU AI Act lists certain employment allocation and performance systems as high-risk, requiring assessment if AI influences worker assignments.

risks: A nightly extract can misstate current availability, hours already worked or certificate status.
A technically feasible transfer may be unsafe or unacceptable in practice.
Adding AI recommendations based on behaviour or personal traits can change the system's regulatory classification; human approval alone does not remove that issue.
Availability and assignment arrangements may engage OR rights and AVG/GDPR requirements.
research_questions: Where is authoritative current availability recorded, and can it be reconciled across employees and agency workers?
Can all essential certificate, CAO and rest-period constraints be expressed and checked reliably?
Does scenario preparation save material time once managers confirm live availability and employees discuss transfers?
Would the proposed design influence assignments in a way that invokes EU AI Act high-risk obligations, and what dates apply?

tasks.short: Help managers choose recruiting and retention actions that produce successful hires who stay.

today.trigger: A manager reports hard-to-fill vacancies, weak onboarding, early departures or a seasonal hiring need.
steps: Clarify the business problem and the affected roles, site and shifts.
Review recruiting, onboarding, retention and staffing data.
Speak with managers and employees to test explanations.
Develop actions with recruiting, learning and operations colleagues.
Recommend a programme, agree ownership and review its results.
drudgery: Joining hiring and employment outcomes manually
Collecting the same context from several HR colleagues
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline: eight HRBP hours per programme review. Data preparation and proposal drafting take roughly three hours; consultation, decision-making and evaluation planning take the rest.

lenses.faster: Reusable cohort views and assisted proposal drafting remove much data assembly and first-draft work. Consultation, checking and programme design remain, reducing an illustrative eight-hour review to 5.2 hours.
lenses.autonomous: An agreed cohort review or manager request starts preparation of aggregate evidence and draft programme alternatives. The HRBP leads interpretation and approves the recommendation before budgets, recruiting practices or employee arrangements change.
lenses.ambitious: New service to site operations managers: a monthly hire-to-day-90 improvement clinic that links hiring sources, week-one onboarding and early retention. Demand would grow if managers could receive timely advice without commissioning a separate analysis.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying pipeline tables into proposals. The HRBP gets more time to understand why warehouse hires leave and design practical changes with supervisors and new starters.
lenses.options: Compare changes to shift expectations before offer, buddy support and onboarding capacity using explicit assumptions and costs. These scenarios can change which bottleneck managers choose to address and how they test the intervention.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward improving the whole vacancy-to-day-90 journey across sites. The HRBP gains authority to recommend and run approved small programme pilots, and becomes more expert in interpreting evidence and evaluating interventions.
reach: Absorb the Recruiter's routine hiring-funnel diagnosis after learning Recruitee stage definitions and recruiting operations.
Absorb the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's standard cohort commentary after learning data linkage, small-sample limits and evaluation methods.
Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's onboarding-gap diagnosis after learning Studytube completion data and supervisor sign-off.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP must distinguish data patterns from causes, understand site realities and win agreement on changes managers can deliver. The person decides what is fair, feasible and worth testing.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: programme advice requires interpretation, stakeholder consultation and choices among uncertain interventions; the model supports analysis and drafts while the HRBP leads.

in_practice.trigger: A monthly cohort review or a manager's recruiting or retention problem.
steps: Build approved aggregate cohorts linking Recruitee hires with AFAS tenure and Studytube onboarding completion.
Check data quality and add an agreed supervisor measure of productivity at day 90.
Use the copilot to draft alternative explanations and programme options from the verified evidence.
Test those explanations with managers, new starters and relevant HR specialists.
Approve a pilot with a budget, named owner and evaluation measures.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP validates the interpretation; the authorized manager approves the programme and budget, with OR involvement where arrangements require it.
data_needed: Consistent vacancy, candidate and hire identifiers
Hiring stages, offers and acceptance outcomes
Agreed role-specific productivity criteria and supervisor sign-off
Site, shift and programme costs at an appropriate aggregation level
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint programme register containing cohort definitions, verified evidence, scenario assumptions, approved pilot and evaluation results.

evidence.claim: Microsoft describes AI-supported HR insights and manager access to workforce information.
IBM reports reorganizing HRBPs into functional pods, providing a documented example of HRBP work moving beyond geographic support.
Aggregate programme analysis and draft alternatives are feasible, but neither the 35% saving nor an improvement in 90-day outcomes is established for Noordhaven.

risks: Seasonality, shift mix and labour-market changes can be mistaken for programme effects.
Retention alone does not establish that a hire is productive.
Small cohorts can expose individuals or produce unstable conclusions.
Moving from aggregate programme advice to candidate or employee scoring creates additional discrimination, AVG/GDPR and EU AI Act concerns.
research_questions: Can Recruitee hires be linked reliably to AFAS and Studytube without exposing unnecessary candidate information?
What observable, role-specific measure establishes productivity at day 90?
Are cohort sizes and historical variation sufficient to evaluate a pilot?
Do managers act on the proposed clinics, and do they improve week-one onboarding or successful 90-day outcomes?

tasks.short: Coach managers to interview fairly, give useful feedback and document performance problems properly.

today.trigger: A manager requests help before an interview, appraisal, difficult conversation or performance-documentation step.
steps: Clarify the conversation, desired outcome and manager's experience.
Check the relevant policy, template and any permitted case facts.
Prepare an interview guide, feedback structure or documentation example.
Coach the manager and practise the conversation.
Review the manager's draft and agree appropriate follow-up.
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline: 90 minutes per coaching session, including preparation and draft review. Tailoring materials and examples takes about 40 minutes.

lenses.faster: Draft guides, examples and role-play prompts replace most material preparation, while the HRBP checks substance and coaches the manager. An illustrative 90-minute session becomes 54 minutes including review.
lenses.autonomous: A manager's request starts a draft guide using an approved template and minimized context. The HRBP reviews it and leads practice; the manager owns the real conversation and final wording.
lenses.ambitious: New service to warehouse and transport supervisors: short conversation-practice sessions available around shift handovers. Demand would grow if practice were easier to arrange, because supervisors could seek help before problems become formal cases.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding training decks or correcting boilerplate. The HRBP gets more time to help a hesitant manager become clear, fair and confident.
lenses.options: Practise a direct opening, a questioning opening and a supportive opening against the same situation. The manager can choose a different approach after seeing how each affects clarity, defensiveness and the chance of agreement.
lenses.altitude: The week contains more targeted coaching and fewer generic presentations. The HRBP gains authority to require coaching before specified formal process steps and becomes more expert in manager development and difficult conversations.
reach: Absorb the Learning and Development Specialist's manager microlearning and practice-material drafting after learning instructional design and Studytube publishing.
Absorb the Recruiter's interview-guide preparation after learning structured interviews, job criteria and bias controls.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP must judge whether a manager understands the issue, challenge unfair assumptions and coach authentic delivery. The manager must use their own verified observations and remain accountable for feedback and documentation.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: the HRBP leads coaching and role-play, while the model supplies editable materials and practice responses without evaluating the employee.

in_practice.trigger: A manager books coaching for a defined interview or workplace conversation.
steps: Select an approved guide and supply anonymized or minimum necessary context.
Draft a conversation structure, factual documentation example and practice responses.
Have the HRBP check legal relevance, fairness and the distinction between fact and opinion.
Practise with the manager and revise the approach in the manager's own language.
Have the manager approve their final material and record coaching completion where appropriate.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves training content and case-specific advice; the manager verifies every factual statement before using it in a real conversation or personnel record.
data_needed: Relevant role criteria and policy requirements
Learning objectives and available session time
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube for participation or completion and a restricted SharePoint library for approved materials; avoid retaining unnecessary practice transcripts.

evidence.claim: Workday reports HRBP-built agents for calibration preparation and check-in feedback, with self-reported preparation savings and feedback-quality results.
IBM describes difficult-conversation role-play pilots, although the digest reports no outcome data.
Anecdotal manager accounts describe employees becoming less receptive to AI-written feedback, supporting review for authentic wording.

risks: Polished language can conceal weak evidence or turn opinion into an apparent fact.
Generic wording can reduce trust during a difficult conversation.
Real personnel cases may be disclosed unnecessarily through prompts or retained transcripts.
Using the tool to score employee performance would require a separate high-risk assessment; face or voice emotion inference at work is prohibited.
research_questions: Does preparation time fall while HRBP review and coaching remain effective?
Do supervisors find the practice useful and use wording they can deliver naturally?
Can reviewers detect unsupported allegations and biased interview questions in generated material?
Can most practice use fictional cases, keeping real employee information out of the model?

tasks.short: Design ways for employees to raise concerns and tell us how work is going.

today.trigger: A survey cycle, recurring complaint or proposed policy change creates a need for better employee feedback.
steps: Define which decision the feedback should inform.
Consult employees, site managers and the OR about access and trust.
Design questions, confidential complaint routes and escalation arrangements.
Test the method with office, shift and agency-worker groups.
Agree ownership, privacy safeguards and how results will lead to action.
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline: ten HRBP hours per method-design cycle. Drafting and comparing materials take about four hours; consultation and decisions take the remainder.

lenses.faster: Draft questions, channel comparisons and procedure checklists reduce document preparation. Consultation, testing and privacy decisions remain, taking an illustrative design cycle from ten to seven hours.
lenses.autonomous: An HRBP-defined feedback need starts draft preparation using approved design criteria. The HRBP and relevant decision-makers approve the method, with OR consent where required, before collection begins.
lenses.ambitious: Group served for the first time: agency workers and night shifts receive a trusted route to report site conditions and get a response. Demand would grow if access improved, so Noordhaven must resource follow-up and agree agency responsibilities.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss repeatedly formatting surveys or reconciling procedure drafts. The HRBP gets more time to hear underrepresented groups and make sure raising a concern leads somewhere.
lenses.options: Compare anonymous pulse surveys, confidential case intake and facilitated shift discussions against the intended decision. These alternatives change what people will disclose, what can be followed up and whether the method is suitable for complaints.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward designing trustworthy employee voice and securing responses from accountable managers. The HRBP gains delegated authority to redesign intake and escalation within approved arrangements, becoming more expert in consultation and measurement.
reach: Absorb the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's basic questionnaire and reporting-specification drafting after learning survey validity and disclosure controls.
Absorb the HR Administrator's complaint-intake procedure drafting after learning confidentiality, escalation and record-retention requirements.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP must judge whether people feel safe speaking, hear minority concerns that averages hide and negotiate credible protection and follow-up. The person must distinguish an anonymous survey from a complaint requiring confidential human handling.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: the central work is choosing a trustworthy method with workers and the OR; the model helps draft and compare designs while people lead consultation.

in_practice.trigger: The HRBP defines a feedback question or identifies a gap in complaint access.
steps: Document the decision to inform, intended groups and existing complaint routes.
Draft alternative questions, access channels and response procedures using approved criteria.
Consult the OR, privacy adviser, agencies and representatives of affected shifts.
Test comprehension, access and confidentiality with a small representative group.
Approve the method, named response owners and reporting safeguards before launch.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves the design; management approves resources and responsibilities, and the OR provides consent for arrangements within its statutory consent rights.
systems: Approved Microsoft 365 survey or intake interface
data_needed: Worker groups, languages and access constraints
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint design and consultation register containing approved questions, access tests, OR decisions and response responsibilities; confidential complaints use a separate restricted record.

evidence.claim: Dutch works-council legislation establishes consent rights for relevant personnel-data and employee-monitoring arrangements.
SER advice calls for people affected by AI outcomes to have access to a complaint route.
Models can draft and compare survey and procedure designs, but trust and validity require human consultation; the 30% saving is unvalidated.

risks: Small shift or site groups can make apparently anonymous responses identifiable.
People may confuse anonymous feedback with a confidential complaint that receives individual follow-up.
Poorly worded questions can bias results or exclude workers with limited English or digital access.
More accessible intake can increase unresolved complaints unless managers and agencies commit response capacity.
research_questions: Which worker groups currently lack a safe, practical feedback route?
Can anonymity survive site, shift and worker-category breakdowns at actual response volumes?
What OR consent, privacy assessment and agency agreements does each proposed method need?
Will named owners respond to concerns within agreed times, including increased demand?

tasks.short: Turn employee feedback into a clear management report with actions and owners.

today.trigger: A feedback cycle closes or management requests an employee-satisfaction update.
steps: Collect survey results and permitted summaries of related concerns.
Check response coverage, comparability and disclosure risks.
Calculate results and read comments for themes and exceptions.
Prepare slides or a report with limitations and proposed actions.
Present the findings and agree owners and follow-up.
today.time_sinks: Illustrative baseline: five HRBP hours per report. Cleaning, theme grouping and slide preparation take about three hours; checking, interpretation and discussion take the remainder.

lenses.faster: Deterministic calculations, reusable charts and one comment-summary step remove most manual assembly. Figure checks, interpretation and management discussion remain, reducing an illustrative report from five to two hours.
lenses.autonomous: Closing an approved feedback cycle starts a fixed reporting workflow that calculates safe aggregates and drafts a source-linked narrative. The HRBP approves the report before management receives it.
lenses.ambitious: New service to the three site managers: a monthly employee-voice action review linking concerns to named actions and previous commitments. Demand would grow as reporting gets cheaper, provided there is enough feedback to avoid unsafe or misleading monthly breakdowns.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying charts or reformatting slides. The HRBP gets more time to challenge management's interpretation and make sure reported concerns lead to action.
lenses.options: Compare a site-focused account, a cross-site theme account and an account emphasizing underrepresented groups and uncertainty. These views can change whether management funds one local fix or a wider change.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from producing reports toward interpreting evidence and challenging action progress. The HRBP gains authority to propose action priorities and escalate missed commitments, becoming more expert in measurement and management influence.
reach: Absorb the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's routine satisfaction-report commentary after learning metric definitions, uncertainty and disclosure controls.
Absorb the HR Director's first-draft management presentation after learning executive reporting and action prioritization.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP must judge what findings mean, protect minority voices and distinguish weak evidence from a serious concern. The person challenges managers and secures realistic action commitments.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: deterministic software calculates figures, and one model call turns minimized comments and verified aggregates into a checkable draft inside a fixed report template.

in_practice.trigger: An approved feedback cycle closes and its dataset passes completeness checks.
steps: Load approved responses and permitted concern summaries into the reporting dataset.
Calculate aggregates and suppress unsafe breakdowns using explicit rules.
Remove unnecessary identifiers and generate themes with traceable internal evidence references.
Draft the management narrative and populate a standard presentation with verified figures.
Have the HRBP approve the findings, limitations and proposed actions before release.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP checks every headline figure, important theme and disclosure risk and approves each report before publication.
data_needed: Approved feedback responses and minimized comments
Question wording and comparable prior-period definitions
Previous actions, owners and completion status
Source references for numerical and narrative claims
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint report register containing dataset version, calculation checks, theme references, HRBP edits and approved report; management copies exclude identifiable comments.

evidence.claim: Deterministic reporting plus a model summary of comments is feasible, but the 60% saving is an unvalidated estimate for this recurring report.
Workday's documented HRBP preparation agents support the plausibility of reducing preparation work, although their results concern different workflows.
Dutch works-council legislation is relevant to the underlying personnel-data and monitoring arrangements used for feedback reporting.

risks: A generated theme can overstate prevalence, miss contradictory comments or invent a causal explanation.
Low response rates can produce misleading site comparisons.
Quotes and small-group charts can identify employees even after names are removed.
Employee comments may contain instructions that the summarizer must treat as data rather than follow.
research_questions: Do independent reviewers agree that generated themes reflect the comments, including minority and contradictory views?
Can every numerical claim be reproduced and every material theme traced to permitted evidence?
Are response coverage and confidentiality adequate for the proposed site and shift comparisons?
Does preparation time fall after all checking, corrections and management discussion are included?

role.altitude: The HRBP becomes a partner for manager capability, complex employee cases and the vacancy-to-day-90 journey. Routine policy guidance moves to a controlled front door; HRBPs use explicit delegated rights to resolve routine exceptions, run approved programme pilots and escalate cross-site problems.
reach: HR Administrator: policy-question intake, case-summary preparation and absence-process deadline checks, with training in AFAS, privacy and Wet verbetering poortwachter.
Recruiter: hiring-funnel diagnosis and structured interview-guide preparation, with training in Recruitee definitions and fair selection methods.
Learning and Development Specialist: manager microlearning drafts, onboarding-gap analysis and certificate-gap identification, with training in instructional design and Studytube.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: standard cohort commentary, staffing scenarios and employee-feedback reporting, with training in data quality, uncertainty and disclosure controls.
HR Director: first-draft management presentations and routine action tracking, with clear limits on policy, budget and employment decision authority.
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks cover about 800 of 1,600 annual hours per HRBP. The proposed savings total about 350 hours per HRBP, or about 1,045 hours across three FTE, before using released capacity for new demand; these are pilot estimates, not measured savings or a headcount forecast. Listening, consultation, negotiation, complex employment judgments and manager coaching limit further automation, while integration and content maintenance reduce realized gains.
skills_to_grow: Dutch CAO interpretation, employment documentation and Wet verbetering poortwachter process boundaries
OR consultation and consent procedures for personnel-data arrangements and technology changes
AVG/GDPR data minimization, access control and retention
EU AI Act classification, oversight and applicable implementation dates
Source checking, model-output review and reliable escalation design
Cohort analysis, survey validity and programme evaluation
Manager coaching, mediation and difficult conversations
Constraint-based workforce planning and cross-site negotiation
role.ambitious_version: The three HRBPs provide a coordinated service across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo: accessible policy guidance, shift-compatible manager coaching and a monthly hire-to-day-90 improvement clinic. They use released capacity to improve week-one onboarding and successful 90-day outcomes, measuring questions resolved without HRBP intervention, days from issue raised to resolution, manager satisfaction and whether workers trust the service.
